page: Microsoft Azure D2ns_v6 is a network-optimized virtual machine from the Dnv6 family, powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, this instance provides 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU runs at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and features a 260 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core, and does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, though it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2101.0. Single-threaded operations like gzip compression at 26.86 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 11.76 GB/sec perform at average levels. However, multi-core and memory-bound workloads show significant limitations. The instance exhibits weak multi-core scaling, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 2590.0 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU performance of 1706.89. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with large-block read and write speeds of 17.21 GB/sec and 12.81 GB/sec respectively, leading to lower performance in memory-intensive tasks.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D2ns_v6 offers a low-resource entry point for workloads that require high single-thread CPU speeds and network optimization without the overhead of large multi-core configurations. Due to its dedicated CPU allocation and strong single-core metrics, it is suited for lightweight single-threaded applications, basic web serving, network-heavy microservices, and simple text processing tasks. It is less suitable for parallelized compilation, database operations, or memory-intensive caching layers.
description: Microsoft Azure D2ns_v6 is a network-optimized, general-purpose virtual machine powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, this instance features 2 vCPUs, 8.0 GB of RAM, and no local storage, relying instead on Premium Storage capabilities. Performance benchmarks highlight strong single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2101.0, alongside average single-threaded compression speeds. However, the instance exhibits weak multi-core scaling and low memory bandwidth, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 2590.0 and a large-block read bandwidth of 17.21 GB/sec. Qualitatively, the D2ns_v6 provides a cost-effective option for network-oriented workloads that prioritize single-thread performance over parallel processing, making it suitable for lightweight web serving, microservices, and basic text processing.
